verdict.rationale: Aider can apply a single natural-language instruction across several files at once: you add multiple files to the chat or pass a file list to the scripting API, and one instruction then runs on all of them. It has no documented dedicated bulk or batch mode, and running across many repos or tasks would rely on user-written loops around --message. missing for 10: an explicit bulk/batch operation feature, documented scale limits for large file sets, and independent hands-on corroboration of bulk edits.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can perform bulk operations across many items at once

citations.quote: # This will execute one instruction on those files and then return
It will do that one thing, apply the edits to the files and then exit.
Do this by naming them on the aider command line.
